name: dog_hill
caption: why has this dog sat on the same block for 900 DAYS
logline: A villager kid tries for 900 days to get the dog on the hill to stand up, until the one person it obeys logs back in.
question: why tf has the dog sat on that hill for 900 days?
premise: A tamed wolf has sat on one hilltop block above the village for 900 days, staring at an empty patch of grass beside an old dirt hut. Bones pile up untouched. A villager kid decides to sit with him so he doesn't wait alone.
twist: A sitting dog only stands for its owner, and its owner is a player who logged out on that patch 900 days ago (players come back where they left). 'Buh joined the game': he appears on the patch and the dog stands for the first time. He says 'Sit, boy. I'll be right back.' and logs out again. The dog sits. Day one.

N.name: Pip
N.profile: a bubbly village kid, about nine: fast, bright, energetic; not whispery, breathy or soft
N.on_screen: baby villager (plains), seen in camera shots

Grandpa.name: Grandpa
Grandpa.profile: an old villager who has seen too much; gravelly, slow, gentle, calls everyone kid
Grandpa.on_screen: villager (plains, weaponsmith outfit? no: a nitwit-free elder, the cartographer)

Player.name: Buh
Player.profile: a young man who logged in for a minute between other things; warm, casual, a bit distracted
Player.on_screen: the recording bot, default Steve skin, only in the last 12 s

requests.direction: A quiet hilltop above a village at the end of the day. Pip: a young kid telling a friend a strange, sad story, hushed and earnest, with real pauses. Grandpa: an old man, gravelly and slow, gentle, tired of explaining.
A young man, warm and casual, a little distracted, talking to his dog for a moment before he has to go.

lines.text: The DOG on the hill / hasn't MOVED / in NINE HUNDRED days.
lines.say: The dog on the hill hasn't moved in nine hundred days.

lines.text: Not for RAIN. / Not for THUNDER. / Not even for ZOMBIES.
lines.say: Not for rain. Not for thunder. Not even for zombies.

lines.text: I bring him a BONE / every MORNING. / He never even LOOKS.
lines.say: I bring him a bone every morning. He never even looks.

lines.text: He wears a red COLLAR. / But nobody in the village / OWNS him.
lines.say: He wears a red collar. But nobody in the village owns him.

lines.text: He just stares / at one EMPTY patch / of GRASS.
lines.say: He just stares at one empty patch of grass.

lines.text: And behind him, / an OLD DIRT HUT. / Nobody knows / who BUILT it.
lines.say: And behind him, an old dirt hut. Nobody knows who built it.

lines.text: I tried to make him STAND. / I BEGGED. / He won't BUDGE.
lines.say: I tried to make him stand. I begged. He won't budge.

lines.text: Leave him be, kid. / Only ONE voice / gets him UP.
lines.say: Leave him be, kid. Only one voice gets him up.

lines.direction: half to himself, remembering something far away

lines.text: So every night now, / I sit with him. / Nobody should wait ALONE.
lines.say: So every night now, I sit with him. Nobody should wait alone.

lines.text: Okay. SIT, boy. / I'll be / RIGHT BACK.
lines.say: Okay. Sit, boy. I'll be right back.

hook: why won't this dog stand up?
